Hazardous

/HAZ-er-dus/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Hazardous means involving risk or danger, especially of harm.

Hazardous means involving risk or danger, especially of harm. Black ice made the mountain pass hazardous long after the snowplows had finished their runs.

Worked Example

The summer job posting looked easy: clear brush along the power-line right-of-way. The orientation video said otherwise. Crews faced steep loose slopes, chainsaws, wasp nests, and lines carrying enough current to kill. By the end of the video, Rosa understood why the listing was tagged 'hazardous work' and why the training lasted two full weeks.

Steep slopes, chainsaws, and live power lines all carry a real risk of harm — that combination of dangers is what makes the work hazardous.

How Hazardous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dangerous

dangerous: able to cause harm

risky

risky: carrying a chance of loss or injury

Antonyms

safe

safe: free from danger

secure

secure: protected against harm

How Strong Is It? — risky → hazardous → life-threatening

risky vs. hazardous

risky vs. hazardous: Risky suggests a chance of something going wrong, while hazardous signals genuine danger of harm.

life-threatening vs. hazardous

life-threatening vs. hazardous: Life-threatening is the extreme end of hazardous — danger to survival itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — hazard

Root — hazard: chance, risk (from Arabic az-zahr, 'the dice,' via Old French hasard)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Hazardous began at the gaming table: Arabic az-zahr, 'the dice,' passed into Old French as hasard, a dice game of pure chance, and then into English as hazard — first a gamble, later any source of risk. The word has no other English cognates; its story is the dice game itself.

Use the root in a new word: hazard

Use the root in a new word: hazard: Every hazard on a job site — the word once meant a dice game of pure chance — shares its gambling-born root with hazardous.

Word Building

Word Choice

safety, regulatory

Hazardous describes situations, materials, and conditions that carry a risk of harm before anything bad has happened — unlike devastated (another word in this unit), which describes the aftermath once destruction has already struck.
